headline: LOGISTEC deploys two 120-tonne harbor cranes at Port of Houston's Care Terminal in first phase of multi-stage program
players: LOGISTEC deployed two 120-tonne harbor cranes at Care Terminal at the Port of Houston, operated by Gulf Stream Marine within the LOGISTEC network, describing it as the first phase of a broader multi-stage investment program covering berthing, rail, yard upgrades, expanded storage and improved access. The terminal handles breakbulk and project cargo. CEO Sean Pierce said the cranes strengthen LOGISTEC's long-term Gulf Coast strategy. LOGISTEC Direct connects terminal operations with trucking, rail, warehousing and distribution across 64 North American ports and 87 terminals. No investment amount was disclosed.
why_it_matters: Two 120-tonne cranes give the Houston breakbulk terminal the heavy-lift capability that wins wind components, modular process equipment and oversized project cargo, the highest-rate Gulf categories. Calling it phase one of a multi-stage program shows Blue Wolf funding organic capacity alongside M&A. Capex is undisclosed, so returns can't be run; the phasing suggests staged approval against volumes.
why_you_care: Blue Wolf funding organic capacity on the platform you ran at Rothschild; heavy-lift capability wins the highest-rate Gulf cargo, though undisclosed capex means the phase-one return cannot be run.

headline: MSIP agrees to sell 660MW Bayonne Energy Center to Jupiter Energy Investor after eight-year hold
players: MSIP agreed to sell the Bayonne Energy Center to Jupiter Energy Investor, LLC. Terms undisclosed; close expected in Q3 2026 subject to customary conditions and regulatory approvals. Bayonne is a 660MW dual-fuel facility in Bayonne, New Jersey comprising 10 simple-cycle aeroderivative gas turbines commissioned in 2012, delivering energy, capacity and ancillary services exclusively into NYISO Zone J via a dedicated subsea cable. MSIP acquired the asset in 2018 and managed it through its TigerGenCo platform; Jefferies was lead financial adviser to MSIP.
why_it_matters: MSIP's first disclosed 2026 exit sells a peaker into what looks like the top of the New York capacity cycle, with Zone J tight on data centre load growth and in-city retirements. The dedicated subsea cable is the whole thesis: in-city deliverability from an out-of-city plant, which cannot be replicated. Terms undisclosed, close expected Q3 2026.
why_you_care: MSIP agreed this exit, closing Q3 2026, after eight years; the subsea cable giving in-city Zone J deliverability is the value story to have straight walking in.

headline: Backcast Partners provides debt capital to Sisu Energy & Environmental as AI datacenter demand drives record backlog
players: Backcast Partners announced a debt investment, amount undisclosed, to support growth and expansion at Sisu Energy & Environmental, LLC, a Tulsa, Oklahoma company providing design, engineering, installation and maintenance services for gas turbine exhaust system casings, emissions reduction systems, noise silencers and waste heat mitigation and recovery. Founders John Hare and Phil Childers, who established the business in 2015, retain their ownership stakes and continue leading operations. The company cited a record backlog driven by AI datacenter operators seeking reliable off-grid power infrastructure.
why_it_matters: Backcast announced an undisclosed debt investment in Sisu, the Tulsa maker of gas turbine exhaust casings, emissions systems and waste heat recovery. Founders John Hare and Phil Childers keep their stakes and stay in charge, and record backlog is coming from AI data center operators buying off-grid power. Taking growth debt rather than selling says they see more value ahead, and being financeable without a sale lifts the price of any future control process.
why_you_care: Reads straight into your Sisu/Miratech work: founders taking growth debt rather than selling, with AI datacenter backlog lifting the price of any eventual control process.

headline: KPS Capital Partners agrees majority investment in Jennmar with FalconPoint and CEO retaining significant minority stakes
players: KPS Capital Partners agreed to make a majority equity investment in Jennmar, with FalconPoint Partners and CEO Tony Calandra each retaining a significant minority ownership position; financial terms were not disclosed. Closing was expected in the second quarter of 2026 subject to customary conditions and regulatory approvals. Evercore and Rothschild & Co advised Jennmar and FalconPoint, with Jefferies advising KPS; Lowenstein Sandler and Paul, Weiss acted for Jennmar and FalconPoint and Paul, Weiss for KPS. Weber Mining & Tunnelling operates as a Jennmar affiliate.
why_it_matters: Two sell-side banks, Evercore and Rothschild, signal a broad competitive process rather than a bilateral deal, which is the best read on value given undisclosed terms. FalconPoint rolling a significant minority rather than exiting at the top of the mining-consumables cycle says it sees value left, especially after the July 2025 Weber deal internationalised the platform. KPS buys operational transformation, so expect footprint rationalisation and bolt-ons. Closed June 16-17, 2026, on the guided timetable.
why_you_care: You ran this at Rothschild, advising Jennmar and FalconPoint. It closed June 16-17 on the guided timetable, and FalconPoint's retained minority says the mining-consumables cycle still has value left.

headline: LOGISTEC acquires Logistics Park Dubuque from Alliant Energy's Travero, adding a 100-acre Mississippi River terminal
players: LOGISTEC announced the acquisition of Logistics Park Dubuque, a 100-acre multimodal terminal in East Dubuque, Illinois on the Upper Mississippi River handling bulk and breakbulk commodities via barge, CN rail and truck, from Travero, a subsidiary of Alliant Energy Corporation. Price was not disclosed. Berenson & Company advised LOGISTEC financially with King & Spalding as legal counsel; RJM & Company advised Travero with Chapman & Cutler as counsel. The announcement followed LOGISTEC's separate agreement to acquire the IPA Terminal in Altamira, Mexico.
why_it_matters: East Dubuque gives LOGISTEC CN rail plus Upper Mississippi barge access into Midwest agriculture, steel and energy flows, tying its Gulf Coast and Great Lakes positions together. Buying from a utility parent shedding non-core logistics is a repeatable sourcing channel, and Alliant's willingness to sell suggests more utility-owned terminals could come to market. Undisclosed pricing here and on Altamira means no multiple reference for the roll-up.
why_you_care: Your LOGISTEC/Termont deal, compounding. Utilities shedding non-core terminals is a repeatable sourcing channel worth flagging at MSIP, though undisclosed pricing leaves no multiple for the roll-up.

headline: Lightpath wins GSA Multiple Award Schedule contract, opening federal and 50-state public sector procurement
players: Lightpath was awarded GSA Multiple Award Schedule contract number 47QTCA26D0021, letting federal agencies buy its fibre and connectivity services through GSA eBuy and allowing state, local and education buyers in all 50 states to procure via Cooperative Purchasing. The company cited a network of more than 12,100 route miles connecting 185-plus data centres and 17,500-plus lit locations with bandwidth up to 800 Gbps, serving over 1,000 existing customers. No contract value was disclosed.
why_it_matters: Lightpath won GSA schedule 47QTCA26D0021, letting federal agencies buy through GSA eBuy and state, local and education buyers in all 50 states procure via Cooperative Purchasing. No contract value disclosed, so it is a procurement vehicle rather than booked revenue. It opens long-term, low-churn, low-credit-risk customers for a network of 12,100-plus route miles and dilutes carrier and hyperscale concentration.
why_you_care: Same asset, different lever: a procurement vehicle rather than booked revenue, but it dilutes carrier and hyperscale concentration on the network MSIP already owns.
